settings.name: Name or handle

settings.business_ph: A few kinds of content, e.g.: building in public, AI tools, book notes
settings.cooperation_ph: Courses, consulting, products… used for calls to action

settings.markets_ph: e.g. Xiaohongshu and X; mostly Chinese, English on X
settings.buyer_concerns: What your readers care about most
settings.buyer_concerns_ph: What readers ask, where they get stuck

settings.profile_hint: What you make or sell, and how you differ from competitors.

settings.audience_hint: Who they are, where they are, what they care about.

settings.tone_ph: e.g. casual, direct, a bit self-deprecating, no exclamation marks
settings.brand_hint: Comma-separated. People searching these already want you, so Search doesn't treat them as opportunities. Your site's domain name (e.g. creght) is included automatically.
settings.brand_ph: e.g. Brand name, 品牌中文名
settings.name_ph: The name you use on your platforms
settings.about_hint: Personal stories in articles only come from here; nothing is made up
settings.about_ph: What you have done, e.g.: three years building SaaS, now building products solo
settings.keywords_ph: side projects, indie dev, AI tools
settings.avoid_ph: Topics you avoid, things not to say

content.new_ai_pick: This is new, empty content: run annulo run content.context --input '{}' to see my positioning and the topic pool, pick the topic most worth doing now, rename the content to it, write the requirements into the brief, then make it, with the copy in copy.md.
content.new_ai_note: This is new content: make it from the brief in its folder. Write the copy to copy.md (title and tags in the --- header at the top), and put any images or videos in the folder too.
content.fork_brief: Write a new piece based on "{title}" (leave the original as it is).
content.fork_ai_note: This is new content based on another piece, whose article_id is {source}: use annulo run folder.list to find the original's folder and read its brief and copy; then make this one from its brief, with the copy in copy.md (title and tags in the --- header at the top) and any images or videos in this content's folder. Don't change the original's files. Give it a fitting name (annulo run folder.retitle).
content.no_search_results: No matching content. Try another keyword.
content.revise_req_hint: When AI edits this content's copy ("Ask AI → Work on this", or asking in the chat), it follows these on top of what you ask that time. Put the style to keep and sections not to touch here.
content.topics_one_time_hint: The gray text is your default topic instructions; leave this empty to follow them. For example: only certain kinds of topics this batch, how many, or the title language.
content.title: Content center
content.desc: Topics and content. Each piece holds its brief, copy, images and videos; when you publish, pick what to post and which accounts.
content.no_site: No site channels yet, so finished articles have nowhere to go. Add one under Channels first.
content.no_articles: No content yet. Click "New content": give a subject or draft and let AI make it, or write it yourself.
content.write_notes_ph: What this piece is about: a topic, a few points or a draft (the first line becomes its name). It's saved as the piece's brief. If AI does it and you leave this empty, it picks the topic most worth doing.
content.import_doc_tip: You can also paste a Notion page link to import it as a draft
content.import_doc_hint: This is a Notion link: "Import from Notion" saves the document as a draft (images go to your library); when the document changes, use "Update from document" on the article page.
content.doc_conflict: This piece's body was edited here. Updating from the document replaces the body and title with the document's current content, and the edits here are lost.
content.write_notes_ph_topic: Add points, material or a draft here. Leave empty to write from the topic.
content.write_notes_hint: How it is written (structure, tone, length) always follows your writing instructions:
content.video_hint: Only if you have a video; video platforms (YouTube, Douyin, Bilibili) use it when publishing.
content.revising: Revising per your notes (a minute or two); it will go back to in-review when done.
content.setup_prompt: Following the content-studio skill, set up how articles are published for channel "{name}" (channel id {id}, site_ref {ref}): CMS collection, field mapping and URL path, written to cms_config in the channels table. Then dry-run article {article}; don't actually publish.
content.setup: Have the assistant set up publishing
content.del_confirm: Click again to delete (posts already published are unaffected)
content.offline: Open the back office from Annulo to review and publish.
content.note_hint: Say what to change and how; the assistant revises and resubmits.
content.note_ph: e.g. The intro is too long, lead with the conclusion; add a real example in section 2; no sales pitch at the end
content.topics_empty: No topics yet. Generate a batch, or add a topic you want to write.
content.topic_ph: e.g. 5 mistakes from my first year as an indie developer
content.angle_hint: Who it's for, what problem it solves, how it differs from existing content.
content.writing_pick: The assistant is picking a topic and writing it
content.writing_desc: It'll show up under Content when done, usually in a few minutes; click "View chat" to watch each step.
content.req_hint: The assistant follows these every time it writes copy. Change length, structure, tone or sections to always include — the next piece follows the new version.
content.ask_ai_hint: The AI edits the current version (including your manual edits) and only touches what you mention.
content.ask_ai_hint_dirty: You have unsaved changes; they'll be saved first and the AI will work on the saved version.
content.stale: This piece was just changed elsewhere (the AI finished, for example) and you have unsaved edits here: saving will overwrite those changes.
content.stale_load: Load the latest, discard my edits
content.revising_ai: The AI is revising this piece
content.revising_desc: This page refreshes when it's done, usually in a minute or two; click "View chat" to see what it changed.

geo.req_hint: The assistant follows these every time it writes GEO questions. Change which kinds of questions, the language, or target markets here — the next batch follows the new version.
geo.title: GEO
geo.no_site: No site channels yet. Add one under Channels to check whether AI answers cite you.
geo.desc: When buyers already know you and use ChatGPT to compare suppliers, is what the AI says right? When buyers don't know you yet, who does the AI recommend? Checks run from your computer, on your own network, with the models configured in Annulo, automatically once a week.
geo.no_table: The three GEO tables (geo_questions / geo_runs / geo_results) aren't ready yet. Annulo creates them from the declarations in tables/; refresh in a moment.
geo.no_questions_desc: GEO checks use questions real buyers would ask. Generate a batch from your positioning and site content, then pick the ones to keep.
geo.not_run_desc: Asks each question on every engine that has a provider picked in check settings (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Doubao), from your computer — a few seconds to over a minute each, without the assistant — and records the results.
geo.mentioned_n: {n} more mentioned in the text without a link
geo.rule: "Cited" means the answer links to a page on your site; "Mentioned" means your brand or domain appears in the text without a link — worth adding content for too.
geo.no_detail: This check left no details; it may have failed midway. Have the assistant run it again.
geo.q_hint: Write it the way a buyer would type it into an AI, not as keywords.
geo.q_ph: e.g. Which audiobook app has the most natural voices?
geo.kw_hint: Comma-separated. When this question cites you, these terms are more likely to bring you up in AI answers too.
geo.kw_ph: audiobook app, text to speech, TTS
geo.q_not_run: Not checked yet. Click Re-run check at the top right.
geo.gen_title: Generated {n} questions — pick the ones to add
geo.dedup: You already have {n} questions; duplicates were removed.
geo.eng_desc: Which provider and model configured in Annulo to ask ChatGPT with (it must support the OpenAI Responses API and web search). Providers and keys are managed in Annulo's Settings → Models — nothing to fill in here.
geo.eng_none: No engine is ready: open check settings and pick a provider
geo.eng_legacy: With no provider, the old local secret {key} is used
geo.eng_builtin: Works once signed in to creght, billed in AI credits
geo.answer_old: This is an older check that kept only the first 800 characters; re-run to see the full answer.
geo.no_urls: The answer didn't cite any URLs.
geo.run_detail: Open to see each question's answer and citations in this check
geo.run_hint: Each question takes half a minute to over a minute; checked automatically every week
geo.s1_desc: Once buyers know your company name, products or website, they ask AI to research and compare. Here are ChatGPT's answers word for word, with the URLs they cite: you judge whether they're right (the data in the system may be out of date too); mark anything wrong and the assistant traces where it came from.
geo.brand_empty_desc: Generate the questions buyers ask once they know you (what the company does, which products, MOQ and certifications, the website…) from the company name, brand terms and products in "Company & products", in the language of your target markets.
geo.s2_desc: Which sites the AI cites when buyers who don't know you yet ask questions, and whether it cites yours (visibility). Who gets cited depends largely on page quality and ranking, much like Google — compare with the Google ranking and your articles under each question.
geo.sites_title: Sites cited most in AI answers ({n} questions)
geo.hint_no_rank: Your site doesn't rank on Google for these words yet
geo.hint_no_article: No article on your site answers this yet
geo.report_ph: Write what the AI got wrong and what is actually true, e.g. we have 12 products, not 3; the MOQ is 300 pcs.
geo.report_hint: The assistant traces where that came from (your site isn't clear, another page is outdated, or your data isn't updated) and writes how to fix it
geo.no_searches: This answer didn't search the web.
geo.checking_bg_hint: Started by the schedule or an earlier page; {n} done so far — each one shows up here as it finishes
geo.vis_rule: Visibility = questions whose answer cites your site ÷ questions in this part (brand questions excluded)
geo.eng_search_only: Only models that can search the web; empty = {v}
geo.eng_search_models: Models that can search the web:
geo.ask_hint: Starts a new chat: the assistant looks into it with this answer, the pages it cited, other AIs’ answers and your data, and saves its conclusion here.
geo.ask_how: How do we get it to recommend us for this question?
geo.ask_ph: e.g. Where does this claim come from? What is wrong and what is true?
geo.ask_ph_rec: e.g. Why did it recommend these and not us? What content are we missing?
geo.ask_title: What do you want to ask? (about this {engine} answer)
geo.ask_why: Why doesn't it cite our site?
geo.brand_dialog_desc: No AI: uses the name and topics in "My positioning" with questions readers often ask (who is this, what do they write about, what have they made, where is their site…). Below are the ones not in your question list yet; tick the ones to add.
geo.brand_none_left: Every common question your current positioning can produce is already in the list. Check back after you change your positioning.
geo.desc2: Whether each AI gets you right when readers who already know you ask about you, and who the AI recommends when people who don't know you yet ask. Checks run on this computer, can ask ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Doubao and others at once, and repeat weekly.
geo.eng_desc2: Each one you turn on gets asked, all at the same time. Web versions ask in your own Chrome (with the accounts you are signed in to; needs the Annulo browser extension), so you see what readers really see; API versions use the models you set up in Annulo.
geo.eng_none2: No AI is turned on for checks
geo.eng_not_tested: Not tried yet: the first time, Chrome asks you to allow it
geo.gen_desc: Hand it to the assistant on the right: it reads your positioning and site, writes questions readers who don't know you yet would ask AI (without your name), and saves them for the next check. Follow along in the chat on the right.
geo.m_brand_legend: "New": you haven’t read this answer yet (opening the row marks it read). "Wrong": you marked it wrong. Green dot: the answer cites your site.
geo.m_col_off: {name} (turned off in check settings; showing the last results)
geo.m_no_cols: No AI is turned on for checks yet.
geo.m_rec_legend: ✓ cites your site   ◐ mentions you without a link   · neither   – not asked yet   ↑↓ more / fewer than this AI’s last check. Column headers show how many recommendation questions cited you in that AI’s latest check. Click a cell to read that answer and its sources.
geo.m_reported_n: {n} marked wrong, not looked into yet
geo.m_vis_title: Latest: recommendation questions citing you {c}/{n}, visibility {v}%
geo.pick_engine_first: No AI turned on yet: in "Check settings", turn on the ones your readers use (ChatGPT for most of the world, Doubao or DeepSeek in China).
geo.run_hint2: The AIs you turned on are asked at the same time, half a minute to a minute or more per question; checks also run automatically once a week.
geo.s1_desc2: Once readers know your name, handle or site, they ask AI about you. Each row is a question and each column an AI: "New" means you haven't read this answer yet; open a row to compare the answers side by side, and ask the assistant under an answer if something is wrong or unclear.
geo.step_no_query: (this AI does not show its search terms)
geo.sum_lost: {n} questions no longer cite your site
geo.sum_no_rec: No recommendation questions yet, so there's no way to tell whether AI recommends you to people who don't know you.
geo.topic_one_desc: Hands off to the assistant on the right: turns “{q}” into a topic in Website articles, ready to write an article so AI cites you. Follow along in the chat on the right.
geo.topics_desc: Hands off to the assistant on the right: turns the {n} questions where AI doesn’t cite your site into topics in Website articles, ready to write articles. Follow along in the chat on the right.
geo.topics_req_hint: The assistant follows this every time it suggests topics (the same one "Suggest topics" uses in Website articles).
geo.q_ph_commercial: e.g. Who are good creators or courses for learning [topic]?
geo.q_ph_comparison: e.g. For [topic], who explains it better, A or B?
geo.q_ph_informational: e.g. How do I get started with [topic]?
geo.sum_brand: {n} brand questions; {c} answers cited your site
geo.sum_rec: {n} recommendation questions; {c} cited your site; visibility {v}%
geo.eng_cli: Local agent, uses its own account and web search
geo.eng_cli_hint: Searches with the local Codex and the account it is signed in with, no credits used. Each question takes a minute or two, and this computer has to be on.
geo.eng_cli_claude_hint: Searches with the local Claude Code, no credits used. It's Anthropic's model and search, so results show whether Claude recommends you, not ChatGPT. Each question takes a minute or two, and this computer has to be on.

social.media_either: Up to {n} images or 1 video, not both
social.no_posts_in_range: No posts published in the last {n} days.
social.all_posts_hint: Numbers are from the latest collection; click a column header to sort by it.
social.title: Social
social.desc: Manage accounts, sign-in, and data collection here. Edit, review, and publish in Content.

Add content to page {page} on channel "{name}" ({site}) following the points below (search_pages id {id}). It averages position {pos} on Google, just short of page one; it needs to fully answer what people searching these terms want to know.

{brief}

How: pull the channel site to $HOME/.shuttle/sites/{site_id} the way the site-audit / ops-backend skills describe (creght pull if it's already there), then edit this page per the points: add sections and an FAQ, and add links to it from the pages listed under internal links. Don't change the page URL, and don't invent facts that aren't on the page or in the project profile (for points that need input from me, ask first or leave them marked).

audit.sg_indexing_do: Pages Google hasn't indexed never show up in search, so nothing else matters until they are. Work through the reasons below: add substance to thin pages, link to unlinked ones, fix wrong canonicals and noindex tags, then request indexing in Search Console.
audit.sg_broken_do: Dead pages and links through redirects waste Google's crawl and lose visitors. Point links at the final address, remove dead ones, and keep only working pages in the sitemap.
audit.sg_content: Make every page substantial and distinct
audit.sg_content_do: Thin content, repeated titles and descriptions, and several pages chasing one keyword leave Google unsure which page to rank. Give articles the specifics readers want (examples, steps, FAQs), and merge or differentiate duplicates.
audit.sg_links_do: Google treats pages nothing links to as unimportant. Link them from the homepage, category pages and related articles, and add linked pages to the sitemap.
audit.sg_onpage_do: Titles and descriptions decide what readers see in search results and whether they click. Give each page a title and description that say what it covers with its main keyword, one H1 per page, and alt text on images.
audit.sg_speed_do: Slow pages hurt rankings and reading: compress large images, drop unused scripts, and check that pages work on phones.
audit.sg_international_do: Add hreflang to each language version and lang on <html> so Google shows readers in each region the right language.
audit.sg_ai: Make the site readable for AI search
audit.sg_ai_do: Allow AI search crawlers and add llms.txt and structured data so ChatGPT and Perplexity cite your site in answers.
audit.plan_desc: Rules can only check whether something exists. Have AI actually read a few pages of each kind (home, article list, articles, about) and log what's poorly written as issues, then write an optimization plan ordered by priority.
audit.plan_at_stale: Reviewed {when}; the site has been checked again since — consider reviewing again
audit.plan_req_hint: How the plan is structured, how detailed, which pages to focus on. Edit here and the next review follows it.
audit.sg_domain_do: Links and structured data still use other domains of this site (old system domain, preview, the www/non-www twin), splitting ranking signals across addresses. Use the main domain everywhere and redirect the others to it.
audit.sg_review_do: AI read a few pages of each kind and found problems rules can't catch (whether titles say who it's for, whether intros are boilerplate, whether articles are specific enough). Each one notes the pages, the original text and what to change it to.
